 Through :- Mr. D S Chauhan Advocate with  Ms. Damini Chauhan, Advocate CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M A CHOWDHARY, JUDGE  JUDGMENT 1.

Appellant, through the medium of this Civil First Miscellaneous Appeal in terms of Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeks modification of the Award dated January 18, 2012 to enhance the amount of compensation, passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Jammu in File No.
459/Claim titled "S.Manjit Singh vs Mohd Ibraheim Bandey & Ors", whereby the appellant as claimant had been granted an amount of 2,00,000/- for his disability suffered in a vehicular accident on 23.03.2005 at Civil Secretariat Road, Srinagar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. The impugned award has been assailed on the grounds that the claimant had led specific evidence that his income had been adversely effected to the extent of  1500/- which means that his salary was not enhanced after the date of accident as was done in the case of his colleagues and he was getting the same salary as before his accident; that the learned Tribunal had wrongly interpreted that due to no reduction in his salary, the claimant had not suffered any loss; that no compensation S.Manjit Singh vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70329359/
1 had been awarded to the appellant-claimant for the period of treatment and the period for which the appellant could not attend his duties because of the injuries/disablement though he had been on bed rest as advised by the doctors w.e.f 23.03.2005 to 03.08.2005 for which leave had been sanctioned by the Department in his favour, as such, he was entitled to compensation by way of leave encashment for the aforesaid period which has not been awarded by the Tribunal; that the appellant had suffered a lot and underwent huge pain and suffering because of the injuries suffered by him;
that he also suffered disfigurement of his face because of which he has been confined to the four walls of his house and could not attend any function, ceremony and other activity which adversely affected him as he was facing mental trauma, agony, frustration and humiliation with every passing day but no compensation was awarded in favour of the appellant on that account, despite there being clear evidence in this regard.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has been further pleaded that the appellant had incurred lacs of rupees on his treatment,
medicines, fee of the renowed private doctors of different departments at Jammu and Srinagar,
tests, equipments, transportation, attendants and special diet, however, he could not collect all the vouchers for the expenses incurred by him and it is a pedantic approach to expect an injured who was undergoing lot of trauma could collect and preserve the vouchers with regard to the expenditure incurred by him; that the learned Tribunal had granted a meager amount of compensation of  70,000/- on account of medical expenses, attendant/transportation charges and special diet which is required to be enhanced to  2,00,000/- as per the modest estimation; that the compensation on account of pain and suffering and loss of amenities each is also meager and requires to be enhanced from  65,000/- granted by the Tribunal to at least  3,00,000/- as per the modest estimation.

4. Mr. S.A.Hussain, learned counsel for the appellant while reiterating the grounds taken in the memorandum of appeal argued that no compensation was granted to the appellant under the head 'loss of income' ignoring the evidence that the appellant after sustaining injuries had proceeded on medical leave for a couple of months, as such, he was entitled to the leave encashment and also that he had not been granted enhanced salary as was granted to his other colleagues for his disability.

He has also argued that the Tribunal has granted meager amounts of  65,000/- under each of heads of 'pain and suffering' and 'loss of amenities' though the appellant had suffered 30% of permanent disability to one of his eye losing all the amenities of life, besides suffering pain.

He has relied upon the law laid down by the Apex Court in a case titled "Rekha Jain vs National Insurance Co. Ltd &
Ors", reported as (2013) 8SCC 389 to buttress his arguments.

entities.text:
Rekha Jain vs National Insurance Co. Ltd &
Ors", reported as (2013) 8SCC 389
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was finally prayed that the amount of compensation be enhanced and the impugned award be modified.

5. Mr. D.S.Chauhan, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company, ex-adverso, argued that the appellant has filed this appeal merely on his assumptions on hypothetical grounds stating that he was not promoted for his disability and that he had been disfigured.

He further argued that the judgment relied upon by learned counsel for the appellant in Rekha Jain's case (supra) is not simply applicable to the appellant's case for the reason that in that case the claimant Rekha Jain had suffered disablement and disfigurement of her face and the Apex Court had taken 100% of her functional disablement in view of her vocation as an actress and the appellant who was a policeman and continued in his job even after the disablement having been caused in the accident, had not suffered any loss of income on any count.

He further argued that the appellant had failed to S.Manjit Singh vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70329359/
2 substantiate on the basis of any evidence as to whether he had not been promoted or granted increments by the J&K Police with whom he was working as an employee for the disability he had suffered.

entities.text: S.Manjit Singh vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was finally argued that the impugned award passed by the Tribunal perfectly in consonance with law, does not call for any interference for enhancement of the compensation and prayed that the appeal being devoid of any merit and substance be dismissed.

6. The appellant, on the date when he met with an accident resulting to his disablement, was working as Assistant Sub-Inspector in J&K Police with monthly salary of 14,105/- and though he pleaded that he had been denied promotion adversely effecting his monthly salary to the extent of 1500/- but he could not produce any documentary evidence in this regard either before Tribunal or this Court, that he had been denied promotion or that his juniors had been promoted superseding him for his disablement, therefore, no loss of income could be stated to have been caused to the appellant during his service in the Police and the Tribunal has rightly held that due to the disability incurred by him, the claimant had not suffered any loss of income.
7.

The learned Tribunal has observed that the claimant had remained hospitalized and had received fracture on his temporal region and ribs besides the injuries on his eyes, ears and nose and the appellant could have been confined to bed for a considerable period of time, as such, a lump-sum amount of  20,000/- was awarded on account of attendant/transportation charges.
The medical expenses were also assessed for want of vouchers to an amount of 30,000/- only besides special diet charges of 20,000/-.
The compensation on account of 'pain and sufferings' and 'loss of amenities of life'was also assessed as  65,000/- under each of the heads.

8. Having regard to the permanent disablement of 30% in one of the eyes, injuries received in temporal region, face, ear, nose and ribs, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal has granted compensation on lower side, which requires to be enhanced.
Viewed thus, the impugned Award is modified as under:
S.No. Granted by Tribunal Modified by this Cour  1. For Pain and Sufferings :65,000/- For Pain and Sufferin  2. For loss of amenities of life :65,000/- For loss of amenities
3 . Medical expenses :30,000/- Medical expenses
4 . Attendant/Transport Charges :20,000/- Attendant/Transport C  5. Special diet charges :20,000/- Special diet charges
Total: : 2,00,000/- Total

The amount of compensation shall be paid to the appellant/claimant by the respondent/insurer along with simple interest @7.50% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition, until its realization.
The requisite court fee shall be first charge on the amount of compensation.
9. The appeal is, thus, allowed and the impugned Award is modified in the aforesaid terms.
10. Tribunal Record along with a copy of this judgment be sent down forthwith for information and compliance.
